chunks: Yunus narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from al-Ala' ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about a man who travels on a road of the Muslims upon his animal, so it hits with its leg.

So he (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no liability upon him for what it hits with its leg, and there is liability upon him for what it hits with its hand, and when it stops, then upon him is what it hits with its hand and its leg, and if he is driving it, then upon him is what it hits with its hand and its leg as well.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ: there is no liability upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on liability when an animal strikes a pedestrian?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the jurisprudence of *daman* (liability) by distinguishing between an animal's natural gait and its directed movement, establishing that the owner is only liable for damage caused by the 'hand' (active control) unless the animal is stopped or being driven. This ruling reflects the Shia legal principle that liability attaches to the owner's agency or negligence, a concept further refined in later juristic works regarding *khata'* (mistake) versus *'amd* (intent).

en.hubeali:
Yunus, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Al A’ala Bin Al Fazl,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> being asked about a man who travelled upon a road from the Muslim roads upon his animal, so it hit someone with its (hind) legs.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon him what it hits by its (hind) legs, and when he pauses it, so upon him is what it hits by its hands (front legs) and its (hind) legs, and even if he is ushering it, so upon him is what it hits by its hands (front legs) and its (hind) legs, as well’.
